question: Researchers from which Indian institute developed an advanced agricultural robot designed to detect plant diseases and apply pesticides precisely?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Indian Institute of Technology Kharagpur (IIT-KGP)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Researchers from the Indian Institute of Technology Kharagpur (IIT-KGP) have developed an advanced agricultural robot to assist farmers in precise detection and management of plant diseases.
 
• This robot integrates artificial intelligence (AI) and computer vision technologies to identify diseased plants and apply pesticides only to the affected areas, reducing chemical usage.
 
• The robot is designed to work autonomously, ensuring efficient disease detection and cost-effective pest management in large agricultural fields.
 
• It aligns with India's goal of promoting sustainable agriculture by minimizing the environmental impact of pesticide usage.
 
• Such innovations aim to enhance productivity and reduce manual labor while addressing the challenges faced by farmers due to plant diseases.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indian Institute of Technology Delhi (IIT-D):**

 
 
• IIT Delhi is known for its cutting-edge research and contributions to various fields like engineering, computer science, and sustainability.
 
• One of its notable achievements includes the development of low-cost ventilators during the COVID-19 pandemic.
 
• While it works on projects in agricultural technology, it is not responsible for the development of this specific robot.
 
 
 
• **Indian Institute of Technology Bombay (IIT-B):**
 
 
• IIT Bombay has expertise in robotics, AI, and machine learning applications across industries, including healthcare and manufacturing.
 
• It has developed several autonomous robots, such as those for underwater exploration and disaster response, but not specifically for plant disease detection.
 
 
 
• **Indian Institute of Technology Madras (IIT-M):**
 
 
• IIT Madras is a leader in AI-driven projects and sustainable technologies, with significant contributions to agricultural mechanization and renewable energy.
 
• One of its notable projects includes developing solar-powered agricultural tools for rural India.
 
• However, this specific robot for detecting plant diseases was not developed by IIT Madras.
